react_result.final_narrative_text: Multi-paradigm enrichment across RaMP multi-DB ORA and Mummichog m/z-network analysis converged on two major pathway clusters. The dominant signal is Galactose Metabolism (SMPDB:SMP00043, KEGG:hsa00052, MUMM:galactose_metabolism), where four of the seven input metabolites — galactinol, sucrose, myo-inositol, and glycerol — produced an FDR of 2.83e-11 in ORA and a p-value of 0.007 in Mummichog, representing a cross-paradigm winner. Galactinol (KEGG:C01235) is the pathway-specific driver; it is not an upstream precursor but the characteristic raffinose-family metabolite of galactose catabolism. 8(S)-HPETE (KEGG:C14823) independently drove Arachidonic Acid Metabolism (MUMM:arachidonic_acid_metabolism, rank 6, p=0.022) — a result inaccessible to the ORA tools because C14823 lacks annotation in their pathway databases. Glycerol (KEGG:C00116) bridges both clusters as a shared compound. Dopamine (KEGG:C03758) and D-glucose (KEGG:C00221) appear in secondary ORA hits (GPCR downstream signalling, WP:WP3604) and Mummichog hexose/phosphatidylinositol modules respectively. The combined evidence suggests that treatment most strongly perturbs galactose catabolism and, separately, the 12-lipoxygenase branch of eicosanoid synthesis where 8(S)-HPETE is the primary enzymatic product.
